memory_update.text: CRWV should remain the reference benchmark for specialized AI cloud capacity, but its high attention and large market cap mean it should not dominate the underfollowed discovery lane.

IREN has become a direct AI cloud capacity candidate because of disclosed NVIDIA/Microsoft-linked GPU cloud contracts and secured-power expansion claims; key risk is execution, financing, and concentration.
APLD maps to the power-to-AI-factory infrastructure layer rather than pure GPU cloud ownership; verify leases, tenant quality, project finance, and delivery milestones.

BTDR is a speculative shadow candidate: strong power-site optionality and early AI cloud disclosures, but AI revenue and customer proof need much stronger verification before advancing to later Serenity layers.

Potential next-pass names not included due to 4-candidate limit: HUT, WULF, NBIS, and possibly CORZ depending on CoreWeave transaction status and listing availability. These should be checked in a follow-up infrastructure/conversion pass.

node: Specialized AI cloud and scarce compute capacity providers
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the specialized AI cloud capacity node found a two-lane universe: CoreWeave as the obvious public reference anchor, and IREN, Applied Digital, and Bitdeer as less traditional public-market mappings where the scarce asset may be powered sites, AI data-center campuses, GPU deployment capability, and customer-contracted compute capacity rather than GPU ownership alone. The underfollowed lane is not low-risk: several names are former or current crypto-mining infrastructure companies pivoting into AI/HPC, so later layers must verify contracted capacity, counterparty quality, financing terms, utilization, power availability, depreciation exposure, and whether AI-cloud economics are durable after hyperscalers expand internal capacity.
